title: Lifetime ISA: Pay In £4,000, Take It Out Early, Get Back £3,750 🏠💷 #shorts
description:
Put £4,000 in a Lifetime ISA, take it out early, and you get back £3,750: £250 less than you paid in.

The government adds a 25% bonus on what you pay in (up to £4,000 a year, so up to £1,000 of bonus), so £4,000 becomes a £5,000 pot. But the 25% withdrawal charge comes off the whole amount you take out: 25% of £5,000 is £1,250. That takes back the £1,000 bonus, plus £250 of your own money: 6.25% of the £4,000 you paid in.

One thing people miss: there's no charge on a first home costing up to £450,000 (bought at least 12 months after your first payment, through a conveyancer or solicitor, with a mortgage), from age 60, or if you're terminally ill. Above £450,000, even a first home pays the 25% charge.

The government plans to replace the Lifetime ISA with a new First Time Buyer ISA (no launch date yet); until then, existing Lifetime ISAs keep the current rules.

Sources: https://www.gov.uk/lifetime-isa/summary · https://www.gov.uk/lifetime-isa/withdrawing-money-from-your-lifetime-isa · https://www.gov.uk/guidance/lifetime-isa-withdrawal-charges-and-charge-free-withdrawals · https://assets.publishing.service.gov.uk/media/6a33c4586422bec01b117765/FTB_ISA_Condoc.pdf

Charge-free: first home ≤ £450,000 (12+ months after first payment, via conveyancer, with a mortgage), age 60+, terminal illness (<12 months to live).
